newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Inespal wants cheaper electricity provider.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Inespal wants cheaper electricity provider.

text.p: Spanish aluminium firm Inespal wants to contract a new electricity provider, perhaps even a foreign one, in order to reduce its power costs, a spokeswoman told Reuters on Monday.

In a report on Monday, financial daily Expansion said that Inespal, along with two other heavy users of electricity -- zinc producer Asturiana de Zinc and CSI Corporacion siderurgica -- would back a big new firm in the electricity sector.
But the spokeswoman said Inespal was simply seeking lower emergy costs, not planning investment in the electricity sector.

"There have been contacts with foreign companies, as we are looking for a cheaper electricity provider, but Inespal hasn't backed anything and, above all, it would not invest a single peseta," she said.
Only after a new legal framework is in place may Spanish companies buy electricity from foreigners.
At the Industry Ministry no one was immediately available to comment.
Primary aluminium production is highly energy intensive and state-owned Inespal, the largest single consumer in Spain, is already paying partial reduced electrical tariffs.
